info.title: Airborne
info.description: Service for managing OTA updates and configurations

get.description: Return the application's current approval policy. An absent row returns disabled, empty rosters, a 24-hour TTL and emergency rollback enabled.

put.description: Replace the application's approval policy. Only actual organisation owners/admins may edit it. Roster identities must be enabled Keycloak users with app access and ordinary release permissions. Enabling requires at least two distinct subjects and a different eligible checker for each maker. Returns 409 until the operator deployment readiness fence is attested after all old instances and writes are drained.

get.description: List the newest deployment requests. Status filtering precedes the 1,000-row cap. Omit x-application to list across the organisation, with per-application read filtering.

parameters.name: x-application
parameters.description: Optional: omit x-application to list readable requests across the organisation. Filter is applied before the 1,000 newest-row cap.

schema.description: Optional: omit x-application to list readable requests across the organisation. Filter is applied before the 1,000 newest-row cap.

post.description: Raise an immutable deployment request. The server resolves and freezes the snapshot, hashes it and records the authenticated subject as requester.

get.description: Fetch one request by UUID independently of queue pagination. Both scope headers are required.

post.description: Approve and immediately execute a pending request. The checker must be currently eligible and different from the immutable requester.
Cancel a request. Only its requester may cancel it.
Reject a request. A checker may reject their own request; a reason is required.

get.description: List groups for the organisation in x-organisation. Member applications are filtered to those the caller can read. Requires Bearer authentication.

post.description: Create a group with a name and full member list. Requires Bearer authentication and an x-organisation header. Only organisation admins/owners can create groups.

delete.description: Delete a group by UUID. Requires Bearer authentication and x-organisation. Only organisation admins/owners can delete groups.

put.description: Replace a group's name and complete member list. Requires Bearer authentication and x-organisation. Only organisation admins/owners can update groups.

get.description: List unresolved upstream write outcomes for an application. Requires Bearer authentication, scope headers, and release read access.

post.description: Resolve an unresolved operation after upstream verification. Only organisation owners/admins or super admins may recover. applied needs positive evidence of the expected change, matched through the operation's generated marker in current upstream state or its audit history. did_not_apply needs the experiment and the application's workspace configuration (defaults, contexts, overrides) to be unchanged from the values saved before the write, plus the operator's confirmation that the original request has terminated. A 409 names the changed config keys or contexts: restore them, or finish the intended change and resolve as applied. Operations created before this evidence was saved cannot be resolved as did_not_apply. The reason must not contain the reserved text "Airborne operation". Markers are not authenticated provenance: anyone who can write to Superposition directly can forge one, so restrict direct upstream write access to trusted operators.

get.description: Return the authenticated user's release overview across accessible organisations and applications. No x-organisation or x-application header is required.
Return the ordered audit timeline for a release. Requires Bearer authentication plus x-organisation and x-application headers.

Compute the rollback decision and package/config reconciliation without persisting an operation or changing upstream, audit, journal, or cache state. Requires release read permission and organisation/application scope headers.
Read stored and effective strict serving policy.

put.description: Change strict serving. Requires release update permission. Both directions require set_strict_serving approval when maker-checker is enabled. Payload body is {strict: boolean}, without release_id.

post.description: Read-only evaluation of one context and toss. Returns whether enabling strict serving removes default fallback; this is not a population-wide impact count.

Register a file by URL, recording its metadata and assigning it a version. Pass the organisation and application in the x-organisation and x-application headers. Use this when the file is already hosted somewhere the server can reach; to upload the bytes directly, use UploadFile instead. Requires a bearer token.

get.description: List all organisations the authenticated user belongs to, along with their applications and the caller's access level in each. Requires a bearer token.

post.description: Create a new application inside an organisation. Pass the target organisation in the x-organisation header. Returns the created application and the caller's access levels. Requires a bearer token.

Create a targeting dimension (standard or cohort) that releases can be targeted against. Pass the organisation and application in the x-organisation and x-application headers. Requires a bearer token.

get.description: List the targeting dimensions defined for an application, in priority order, with pagination. Pass the organisation and application in the x-organisation and x-application headers. Requires a bearer token.

delete.description: Delete a dimension by name. Pass the organisation and application in the x-organisation and x-application headers. Requires a bearer token.

put.description: Update a dimension, identified by name in the path — for example to change its priority position. Pass the organisation and application in the x-organisation and x-application headers. Requires a bearer token.

post.description: Add an independent inclusive stable major.minor.patch semantic version interval. Prerelease and build metadata bounds return 400 because upstream comparators do not support their precedence. Earlier definitions are unchanged. Enum index zero wins overlaps. Does not alter checkpoint semantics. Requires cohort update permission; unavailable while maker-checker is enabled, like other targeting edits.
Create a new organisation owned by the authenticated user. Returns the created organisation with its (initially empty) application list and the caller's access levels. Requires a bearer token.

Submit a request to have an organisation provisioned (for onboarding flows that require manual approval), including contact details and store links. Returns a confirmation message. Requires a bearer token.

Create a package: an index file plus the set of files that make up an OTA bundle. Pass the organisation and application in the x-organisation and x-application headers. Returns the created package with its assigned version. Requires a bearer token.

Returns 409 if another release is already ongoing for the same dimensions. Requires a bearer token.

get.description: Get a single release by its id, including its config, package, resources, targeting dimensions, and experiment details. Pass the organisation and application in the x-organisation and x-application headers. Requires a bearer token.

post.description: Independently acknowledge the emergency rollback for its source release. Only a different current checker may acknowledge it.

Make one variant of a ramped release permanent. Concluding on an experimental variant promotes the release; concluding on the control variant ends it and leaves the previous release live. Read the variant ids from experiment.experiment_variants on GetRelease. The release must have been ramped first. Unknown release ids return 404. Pass the organisation and application in the x-organisation and x-application headers. Returns 409 when the release is still only created (ramp it first) or has already concluded or been discarded, 409 with "code: unresolved" when an upstream outcome is unknown, and 400 when the chosen variant does not exist. When the application requires approvals, every conclude is refused with 403 "approval_required"; raise a deployment request instead. Requires a bearer token and release conclude permission.

parameters.name: release_id
parameters.description: ID of the release (the experiment id returned by CreateRelease).

schema.description: ID of the release (the experiment id returned by CreateRelease).

post.description: Discard a release that has not been ramped, so it never serves traffic. Only a release in the created state can be discarded; a ramped release must be concluded on "control" or rolled back instead, and a release that is already concluded or discarded returns 409. Unknown release ids return 404. Discarding never needs approval. Pass the organisation and application in the x-organisation and x-application headers. Returns 409 with "code: unresolved" when an upstream outcome is unknown. Requires a bearer token and release discard permission.

parameters.name: release_id
parameters.description: ID of the release (the experiment id returned by CreateRelease).

schema.description: ID of the release (the experiment id returned by CreateRelease).

post.description: Set the share of traffic that receives a release. A release starts at 0% and is not served until it is ramped; the first ramp moves it from created to in progress, and later ramps raise or lower the share. Pass the organisation and application in the x-organisation and x-application headers. Unknown release ids return 404. Values outside 0–50 return 400 before any write is attempted. Explicit upstream 400 and 422 validation rejections for ramps are recorded as not applied and do not pause writes for the application; other uncertain outcomes return 409 with code "unresolved" and own_attempt true, so inspect the real state before retrying and never repeat a committed ramp merely to clear a cache failure. Returns 409 when the release has already concluded or been discarded, and 409 with code "unresolved" when an earlier upstream write for the application still needs recovery; an organisation admin can resolve that operation with ResolveControlCenterOperation. When the application requires approvals, raising traffic (or any ramp of a rollback-sensitive release) is refused with 403 "approval_required"; raise a deployment request instead. Requires a bearer token and release ramp permission.

parameters.name: release_id
parameters.description: ID of the release (the experiment id returned by CreateRelease).

schema.description: ID of the release (the experiment id returned by CreateRelease).

post.description: Roll back a release according to its lifecycle state. Writes are durable and retries of a completed operation return its recorded success, including later unrelated live-release diagnostics. Unknown upstream outcomes return 409 unresolved and require real-state/operator review; changed replacements return 409 replacement_changed and must not be resumed automatically. Re-release only works while the source is the latest live release for its dimensions. Requires Bearer authentication plus x-organisation and x-application; callers need release write/conclude permission.
Optional unverified device reports. 400 drops invalid/expired receipts; 429 retries later; 503 means disabled/unavailable.

Exchange user credentials (client_id and client_secret) for an access token and a refresh token. Public — no auth token required. Call this first, then send the returned access token as a bearer token on subsequent requests.

UnresolvedOperationErrorResponseContent.description: A write has an unknown upstream outcome. Inspect its real state and change history before resolving it; elapsed time alone does not establish rejection. An upstream 4xx is not proof that nothing was written, because the upstream handler can return it after configuration effects. While the operation is unresolved, writes for the application stay paused. When the 409 comes from a recovery attempt it can name the config keys or contexts that changed and must be restored, or finished and resolved as applied.

expected.description: The exact state expected after the upstream write.

own_attempt.description: True when this request itself may have changed upstream state; absent when an earlier write is blocking this request.

refresh_token.description: Token used to obtain a new access token once the current one expires.

refresh_expires_in.description: Lifetime of the refresh token, in seconds.
